findings.evidence: Finite arithmetic example in interfaces.json: pre-witness=0 us, breakpoint=1000 us, dispatch=15000 us, effective resume/stop=50000 us. Dispatch-based elapsed=15000 us passes 20000 us, while actual hold=49000 us does not. This is not a runtime test.
findings.problem: Lines 182-184 describe the selected-hold bound as a pre-instruction witness to release/kill dispatch interval. Dispatch alone is not necessarily the end of a ptrace hold: transport, syscall, signal delivery or scheduling can postpone effective continuation/termination. The stricter pre/post conservative-enclosing-bound requirement at lines 190-196 is sound, but the more specific dispatch wording could be implemented as an undercount.
findings.recommendation: In the prepared target/oracle/receipt contract, use the conservative actual-end bound required by lines 190-196: a post-continuation witness (or demonstrated effective-release upper bound) for resume and independently confirmed target stop/exit for kill, with clock uncertainty included. Retain dispatch as a separate timestamp. Consider a closed validator timing vector where dispatch is timely but effective completion is late or absent; reject the timing claim. If overhead is only conservatively upper-bounded, label it as a bound rather than a measured slowdown.
findings.title: Make the hold-duration endpoint explicit in the executable packet
findings.why_not_a_documentation_blocker: The package already mandates conservative target pre/post witnesses, independent actual-stop evidence and separate review of the exact executable packet. Those requirements admit a safe implementation without changing the design direction or accepting runtime feasibility. This review does not authorize any dispatch-only timing claim.

findings.problem: The frozen base stores all grants in fixture.acl once, deletes users only in live Redis, and authenticates setup in ready(). No reviewed durable ACL helper or postfault read/BOOT role lifecycle exists. Reusing that base sequence for a new restart after measurement retirement would restore forbidden authority. Current cases restart before retirement, so this is not a newly discovered violation in those cases.

proof.description: Independent AST/text checks establish DELUSER/held-disconnect/WRONGPASS with no ACL persistence, no file/dir fsync in initialize, no SAVE/LOAD/SETUSER grant, and setup in ready. Hash-matched Redis source loads ACL before listeners/AOF; an omitted default creates on/nopass/+@all/~*/&*. ACL SAVE does file and directory sync but saves the still-live revoker if called before its deletion. Calling it after deletion cannot assume a surviving admin.

findings.recommendation: For a separately approved corruption-only contract, freeze exactly the explicit deny-all bytes, fixed control-only writer, no-follow/single-link/ownership checks, atomic replacement, successful file+dir sync/readback, writer extinction, then actual all-role live retirement including final revoker/default denial before any fault. All failed prefixes abort the negative while safe cleanup continues. Obtain the owner sequencing interpretation; do not certify this route now. For successful internal-COMMIT restart contracts, durably retire setup while retaining only separately reviewed observation/loading/BOOT roles; never reuse setup-ready or regrant to inspect a failed case.

findings.problem: There is no frozen observer, OCI profile, target identity union, TID-filter generator or instantiated filter, and no demonstrated hardware/capability profile. These are intentionally missing feasibility artifacts, not internally contradictory approval requirements after the parent clarifications. proof.description: The parent explicitly separates static template/generator approval from generated TID-specific bytes and permits only an approved deterministic substitution or per-instantiation decision. It requires all C1 capability sets observed after entrypoint exec and blocks lost SYS_PTRACE or unapproved root/file/ambient/inheritable authority. D01 permits narrowly reviewed hardware debug-state programming and fixed single-step, not GPR/PC/memory edits. The private raw locations file is independently measured at 2,666,992 bytes, exceeding the unchanged 2,097,152-byte limit.

findings.recommendation: Prepare C0-only fixed synthetic target/observer/oracle/validator artifacts with a compact closed manifest and explicit post-entrypoint CapEff/CapPrm/CapInh/CapAmb/CapBnd=0 admission. Bind kernel boot, UID/GID, user namespace inode/maps, PID namespace, exact container/process/main TID/start ticks and executable; invalidate exec/restart/reuse and prevent reattachment to reused TIDs. Freeze audited default-deny OCI and additional-filter template/generator identities plus substitution validation and installation receipts. Treat observer memory reads and debug-register programming as trusted authority. Preserve the independent watchdog, exact owned cleanup, timing/event/read/output budgets and no-fallback failure state. C1 remains a separately gated hypothesis, not part of this GO.

CAP_FIELDS = frozenset(("CapEff", "CapPrm", "CapInh", "CapAmb", "CapBnd"))
def c0_caps_ok(observed):
    return (type(observed) is dict and set(observed) == CAP_FIELDS
            and all(type(v) is int and v == 0 for v in observed.values()))
# Require a post-entrypoint, exact-process observation; a Docker flag is not that receipt.

proof.description: Hash-matched aof.c prints a manifest line at 359 and AOF argv[0] at 1528-1529. The fatal startup path also includes open/I/O errors; exit 1, exit 137, timeout, WRONGPASS, LOADING or socket absence do not distinguish damage. findings.recommendation: Prepare a source-bound closed error-enum/diagnostic receipt contract with explicit input, parse, memory, output, count and time bounds; independent causal process/file/config identity; conservative truncation/overflow behavior; and canary-redaction tests on normal/error/core paths. Default to no raw retention. Any diagnostic exception needs its exact private destination/access/contents/size/expiry/disposal and no reusable authority. Inventory every worker/observer/helper/watchdog/Redis process, named-volume creation identity, private transport and authority-bearing file; stop/wait/remove/independently verify absence. On ownership ambiguity or foreign attachment, block only the unsafe deletion and continue other proven-owned cleanup, naming every unresolved obligation.
